gaps.sentence: It took the committee weeks to wade ___ the paperwork.
gaps.hint: wade ___ = plod through a lot of
gaps.explanation: 'Wade through' = work slowly through a large amount of tedious material.

gaps.sentence: The talks fell ___ when neither side would compromise on fishing rights.
gaps.explanation: 'Fall through' = (a plan or deal) fail to be completed.

gaps.sentence: The publishers are bringing ___ a revised edition in the spring.
gaps.explanation: 'Bring out' = produce and publish a new product or edition.

gaps.sentence: I've mixed ___ the twins' names again.
gaps.explanation: mix up = confuse one thing/person with another.

gaps.sentence: I bumped ___ my neighbour at the dentist's.
gaps.explanation: bump into somebody = meet by chance.

gaps.sentence: She looks ___ on people who disagree with her.
gaps.explanation: look down on = consider inferior (opposite: look up to).

gaps.sentence: They broke ___ after only two years of marriage.
If you don't know the word, look it ___ in a dictionary.
gaps.explanation: look a word up = find it in a dictionary/reference.
